---
title: Set
description: "Unordered membership labels, such as merchant tags."
---

`Set` represents unordered label membership. Suppose a payment dataset
includes merchant tags such as `grocery` and `essential`. In the example
below, these tags add context alongside the amount and merchant identity for
predicting a later dispute; their order carries no meaning.
Use [Category](category.qmd) for one label and
[Branch](branch.qmd) when each item has its own fields or position.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    merchant_tags=rf.Set,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
merchant_tags:
  - grocery
  - essential
disputed: false
```

## Input and options

An Arrow list holds the labels; a scalar label is treated as a one-member set.
Labels may be Boolean, integer, floating-point, string, or binary, with one
compatible Arrow type family per field. Duplicate members collapse, and null
members are ignored, as are NaN members of floating-point sets. An empty list
is valued; a null list has state `null`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p_unavailable` | `0.01` | Training probability of hiding each known positive input member. Reconstruction answers remain intact. |
| `threshold` | `None` | Prediction filter in `[0, 1]`; retain labels whose probability meets it. `None` returns every populated label. |
| `strip` | `False` | Trim surrounding whitespace from string labels before vocabulary lookup. |
| `cased` | `True` | `False` lowercases string labels before lookup. Vocabulary snapshots and written labels hold the folded form; other label types are unaffected. |

See [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options)
for target and embedding configuration.

## Vocabulary and learning

Vocabulary storage grows automatically, with no size option to configure.
The shared [Online vocabulary](../concepts/online-vocabulary.qmd) contract covers
admission order, growth and state preservation, supported training strategies,
and checkpoint reuse.

The training process binds batch-local member dictionaries before forward,
growing embedding rows, membership width, counters, and decoder rows as needed.
Validation, test, and prediction reuse the frozen mapping. For an
application-supplied trained `model`:

```python
labels = rf.Set.vocabulary(model, rf.Address("merchant_tags"))
```

This tuple snapshot lists populated labels in index order. It also accepts a
preprocessor's `encoding_context`; consult established vocabularies for
inference preprocessing, not to decide which training labels may be learned.

Content lists each set's distinct known member identities as compact indices,
padded to the widest set in the batch, plus a count of distinct unavailable
members; dense membership over the allocation forms only where the
reconstruction loss needs it. Unknown identities take no index; duplicates and
member order do not affect either representation, and storage grows with
observed members rather than with the vocabulary. The encoder averages known
member embeddings and adds a learned contribution when **any** member is
unavailable, plus the value-state embedding. That contribution starts at zero;
real or simulated OOV training teaches it. It distinguishes unavailable
membership from genuinely empty input without inventing unknown identities.

Reconstruction combines unweighted state classification with binary cross
entropy over **populated** labels in valued target sets. Unallocated slots are
not negative examples of future labels. Complete set annotations are assumed:
known positives and known negatives remain supervised even in a partial-OOV
or all-OOV set. Unknown members cannot supply identity-specific positives.
An empty set supplies known negatives; null is a separate state.

Metrics use a fixed `0.5` cutoff. Training scores describe the latest batch;
validation and test use summed counts across batches and DDP ranks:

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `targets.known`, `targets.unavailable` | Counts of distinct positive memberships per selected valued set, summed across observations. |
| `coverage.content` | Known positive memberships / all positive memberships. |
| `sets.valued`, `sets.complete`, `coverage.set` | Selected valued sets, sets with no unknown members, and their complete fraction. Empty sets are complete. |
| `loss.content`, `accuracy.content` | BCE and bit accuracy over populated membership slots only. |
| `accuracy.set` | Exact-set accuracy; any unknown target member makes the complete answer unrecoverable. |
| `precision.content`, `recall.content`, `f1.content` | Micro membership scores on known labels. |
| `recall.all`, `f1.all` | Micro scores also counting unknown target members as missed positives. |

An empty denominator yields `NaN`, not perfect reconstruction. Bit accuracy
alone can still be misleading for sparse sets; examine F1, exact-set accuracy,
and coverage together. Output `threshold` does not change these metrics.

[P063](../evidence/vocabulary/set-reconstruction-coverage.py) tests probability
preservation and coverage; [P064](../evidence/vocabulary/set-unavailable-fallback.py)
tests learning the empty/unknown distinction.

## Prediction

`content` is a list of `value` / `probability` structs, with string labels and
independent membership probabilities. Only populated vocabulary entries appear.
The configured threshold filters this list; it changes neither training metrics
nor the decoder computation over the current allocation.

See the [prediction envelope](../reference/prediction-output.qmd) for shared
state probabilities, `inferred`, and repeated shapes.
